question: What has each of the five actually disclosed about advisor compensation structures?

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that for certain revenue-producing employees in Wealth Management and Investment Management, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link compensation to revenues. It gives no payout percentages in the cited text.

Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley (deferred pay): The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that the Firm sponsors deferred cash-based and stock-based compensation programs including for Wealth Management financial advisors, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions. Advisor deferred compensation is generally 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) repeats this language.

Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley (deferred pay accounting): The 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-05) says DCP compensation expense is based on the notional award value adjusted for changes in the fair value of the investments employees select, and is recognized over the vesting period. Beginning in 1Q26 the Firm hedges certain DCP awards with derivatives and no longer presents non-GAAP measures excluding DCP (1Q26 earnings release, 2026-04-15).

Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley (conflicts disclosure): Morgan Stanley's Form ADV (published 2026-11-04) states that Financial Advisors and their Branch Managers receive no additional compensation from the fund-related payments Morgan Stanley receives.

Advisor compensation structure - Merrill: Merrill's Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) says the advisor compensation structure creates conflicts of interest. It says advisors earn compensation based on revenue Merrill earns from the Merrill Lynch Fee in the Program, on other fees and costs, on Sales Charges in brokerage accounts, and on referrals to Affiliates including banking products.

Advisor compensation structure - Merrill (awards): Merrill's Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) says advisors are eligible for a compensation award, payable over a defined period, from an incentive program currently based on meeting prior-year growth targets in new households and in assets and liabilities. An advisor is subject to a reduction in their incentive compensation grid if they fail to achieve growth in assets and liabilities for two consecutive years. The ADV says Merrill approves its compensation program year to year and the criteria can change. Advisors receive no additional compensation for advisory client assets held in the Cash Sweep Program.

Advisor compensation structure - Merrill (management pay): Merrill's Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) says field management compensation is based partly on revenues to Merrill and on advisors meeting strategic goals, and that management incentive compensation reflects the profitability of Merrill and BofA Corp. Merrill itself acknowledges a resulting conflict of interest.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes a firm-wide employee compensation package of base pay plus performance-based incentive pay, equity awards, recognition awards and benefits. This text is not specific to financial consultants or advisors.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab (financial consultants): Schwab Wealth Advisory's Form ADV (published 2026-10-15) says financial consultants (FCs) receive compensation for enrolling clients in the SWA Program and for ongoing service, and that this varies by program or service chosen. Schwab acknowledges FCs may earn more on SWA assets than on commission-based brokerage accounts or certain other advisory programs, a potential conflict of interest. It points to schwab.com/representative-compensation for more.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab (bonus and incentive): The 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-15) says Schwab uses adjusted diluted EPS and return on tangible common equity as performance criteria for employee bonus and certain executive incentive arrangements, with Compensation Committee discretion. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) attributes higher incentive compensation to the Company's financial performance and notes headcount growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab (referral-based): The investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) states that Schwab Advisor Network advisors are independent, not Schwab employees, and pay fees to Schwab in connection with referrals. This is the advisor paying Schwab, not Schwab paying its own advisors.

Advisor compensation structure - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states that financial advisors are generally compensated on a commission basis, subject to a minimum guaranteed salary. It says they may be entitled to additional compensation based on branch office profitability and the Partnership's profitability. The retirement plan consists of a profit-sharing contribution tied to the Partnership's profitability and a 401(k) contribution.

Advisor compensation structure - Edward Jones (variable pay): The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says a significant portion of the Partnership's profits is allocated to variable compensation paid to associates as bonuses and profit sharing, a key component of its performance-based compensation model. It reports variable compensation up 33% in the quarter to $780 and 27% in the first half to $1,528, due to increased branch and Firm profitability.

Advisor compensation structure - Edward Jones (referrals and conflicts): Edward Jones's Form ADV (published 2026-03-27) says Edward Jones and its financial advisors pay third parties for client referrals and leads (paid solicitor arrangements), using flat or subscription fees or ongoing fees as a percentage of advisory program fees. It also says revenue sharing creates additional financial benefits to the firm, its financial advisors and equity owners.

Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (payout ranges): Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists payout by affiliation model: Traditional Employee up to 50%; Advisor Select 70-80% gross payout; Independent Contractor 81% to 90%; Corporate RIA 81% to 90%. For Bank & Credit Union it describes a compensation package from the financial institution, and for RIA & Custody Services compensation is set with the RIA or broker/dealer.

Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (employee vs independent contractor): On the fiscal 2Q26 call (published 2026-04-22), CEO Paul Shoukry said independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their own overhead, real estate and health insurance. He said even the employee side has tiered payout systems, so higher production moves an advisor up the payout grid. Raymond James's Advisor Select page (content as of 2026-03-11) says advisors who run their branch's P&L earn a higher rate on production.

Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (Form ADV): Raymond James's Form ADV (published 2026-09-14) says an advisor's share of the advisory fee can rise with annual revenue generation, and that advisors may share part of their payout with other advisors. Newly affiliated advisors in the Advisor Mastery Program may receive a salary in addition to advisory fees (or in addition to commissions and trails) for a period of time.

Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (retention awards): On the fiscal 4Q25 call (published 2025-10-22), the CFO said fiscal 2025 adjusted compensation expense included amortization of transition assistance for recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors totaling $355 million, up approximately 11% from fiscal 2024.

adjacent.text: Trade press (InvestmentNews, 2026-10-26) reports Morgan Stanley is raising a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027 and that Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses in their 2027 pay plans. It also reports Merrill is leaving its core pay grid unchanged for next year.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative; neither firm's filings in the evidence state these 2027 grid terms.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K reports total compensation and benefits expense of $29,216 million, up 12%, attributed mainly to a higher formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors and higher discretionary incentive compensation in Institutional Securities.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-11-16) says Merrill's returned veteran-broker recruiting came with 'a more aggressive offer', but gives no package terms.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative, and it states no recruiting package terms.

adjacent.text: Trade press (InvestmentNews/Regulation-focused outlet, 2026-08-20) quotes a recruiter saying Schwab offers one of the industry's sweetest W-2 advisor packages, paying salary and bonus for winning client assets.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative; Schwab's own filings in the evidence do not state financial consultant salary or bonus terms.

adjacent.text: Schwab's 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) shows quarterly incentive compensation of $424 million versus $384 million a year earlier, within total compensation and benefits of $1,653 million.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones's 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) reports financial advisor compensation and benefits expense up 18% in the quarter to $2,001 and 16% in the first half to $3,876, attributed to higher revenues on which commissions are earned.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: Payout grids are not public. The formulaic payout percentages and the terms of any recruiting packages are not stated in the evidence.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management advisor recruiting materials or the annual advisor compensation plan communications

gaps.what: Merrill: Payout grids are not public. The grid levels and recruiting package terms are not stated in the evidence; the Form ADV describes only the award structure.
gaps.suggested_source: Merrill advisor recruiting materials or the annual advisor compensation plan documents

gaps.what: Schwab: Payout grids are not public. Financial consultant base salary, bonus formula and referral-pay amounts are not disclosed in the evidence; the Form ADV points to schwab.com/representative-compensation, which is not in the evidence.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab representative compensation web page (schwab.com/representative-compensation) and Form ADV Part 2A

gaps.what: Edward Jones: Payout grids are not public. Commission rates and the formula for branch-profitability compensation are not stated in the evidence.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones Form CRS / representative compensation disclosures, or advisor recruiting materials

gaps.what: Raymond James: Headline payout ranges are published (company recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21); the full payout grid is not public. The 10-K and calls give aggregate retention and transition-assistance amortization ($355 million for fiscal 2025) but not per-advisor terms.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James advisor recruiting team or the payout schedule in advisor affiliation agreements
